title: Retrospective asm audit of all gf2-kernels-simd entry points
description:
Apply the I3 asm-inspection convention (`c3a9a4cb`) retrospectively to every existing SIMD entry point in `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/x86/`. As of session 1, only 2 of ~26+ production SIMD functions have a committed `*.asm.txt` artefact (the `avx2_xor_into`/`avx2_not_into` sample from `c3a9a4cb`). Without retrospective coverage, we ship SIMD code whose actual emitted mnemonics, ILP, register usage, and dispatch opacity are unverified.

## Background

The PPC-spiral epic establishes the asm-artefact convention to enforce proof-of-mnemonic at every spiral step (see `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md` §I3). The convention is gated by `asm-artefact-present` (registered 2026-04-26), which fires on `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/x86/*.rs` modifications. But existing kernels — committed under prior epics (`e095a100` SIMD foundation, plus the per-prime specialisations) — predate the convention. They have no asm artefacts.

The c7791a20 measurement (commit `1a2f6f9`) empirically showed that `OnceLock<Option<&'static LogicalFns>>` of `fn(_,_)` pointers is opaque to LTO regardless of mode (`thin` and `fat` both fail to devirtualize). Every *other* dispatch table in the crate (`Fp65537Fns`, `MersenneFns`, `Gf2mWideFns`, `ClmulFns`) has the same structural shape. Until we look at the asm, we don't know whether they all share the LTO-opacity problem or whether some are reached via a different (LTO-friendly) path.

## Inventory (entry points to cover)

| Module | Entry points | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `avx2.rs` | 9 fns at lines 15, 35, 55, 75, 97, 153, 199, 244, 296 | Logical XOR/AND/OR/NOT/popcount + variants. Already covered: `avx2_xor_into`, `avx2_not_into` |
| `clmul.rs` | `clmul_u64`, `clmul_batch`, AVX-512 variant at line 130, `clmul_barrett_reduce` | Mixed pclmulqdq + vpclmulqdq |
| `fp65537.rs` | `fp65537_batch_mul8`, `fp65537_batch_mul`, `fp65537_batch_add`, `fp65537_batch_sub`, `fp65537_batch_karatsuba`, +1 | Goldilocks-prime kernels |
| `gf2m_wide.rs` | `clmul_wide4_xmm`, `clmul_wide4_ymm` | XMM pclmul + YMM vpclmulqdq |
| `mersenne.rs` | `mersenne31_batch_mul8`, `_batch_mul`, `_batch_mul_add`, `_batch_dot` | Mersenne-31 prime kernels |
| `modem.rs` (line 490, 551) | 2 SIMD fns | (live in the SIMD crate but outside `x86/`; gate doesn't currently apply — check whether to extend) |
| `llr.rs` (line 118) | 1 SIMD fn | Same |

Total: ~26 entry points across 5 `x86/` modules + 2 sibling files.

## Deliverables

1. **Per-module asm artefacts** — one `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/x86/asm/<module>.asm.txt` per source file (or per-fn split if the module is large). Use `dev/scripts/regen-asm.sh` for each. Each header records the commit SHA at regeneration time (`b817e3c` or later).

2. **Audit summary report** — `dev/bench_results/2026-04-26-asm-audit.md` (or whatever date the work lands). One section per module covering:
   - Expected mnemonics per fn (from source: `_mm256_xor_si256` → `vpxor`/`vxorps`, `_mm_clmulepi64_si128` → `pclmulqdq`, etc.)
   - Observed mnemonics (from the artefact)
   - Verdict per fn: **looks correct** / **suspicious** / **clearly broken**
   - For each "suspicious" or worse: short paragraph explaining the concern (register spills, missing-FMA, dispatch opacity, etc.)

3. **LTO-opacity check** — extend the report with a section comparing how each dispatch table (`LogicalFns`, `Fp65537Fns`, `MersenneFns`, `Gf2mWideFns`, `ClmulFns`) is reached at the call site. Use the bench_csv_emitter (or a small harness) to dump asm of the call site (e.g., `gf2_core::kernels::ops::xor_inplace` for `LogicalFns`, the analogous wrapper for each other table) and look for:
   - `OnceLock::get()` followed by `call rax` (opaque pattern)
   - Inlined SIMD mnemonics with no indirect call (LTO-friendly pattern)

   Document whether the opacity problem extends beyond `LogicalFns`. If it does, this confirms `c69d2055`'s scope should expand to all dispatch tables, not just `xor_inplace`.

4. **Follow-up bugs** — for every "suspicious" or "broken" finding, file a `type:bug` issue under `epic:gf2-core-ppc-spiral`, `story:ppc-infrastructure`, with the offending fn, the suspected cause, and the asm evidence cited from the new artefact.

5. **Should `modem.rs` and `llr.rs` SIMD fns be covered by the gate?** — The current `asm-artefact-present.sh` only checks `crates/gf2-kernels-simd/src/x86/*.rs`. The 2 SIMD fns in `modem.rs` (lines 490, 551) and 1 in `llr.rs` (line 118) live outside that path. Decide whether to extend the gate (and if so, in this task or a follow-up).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] Every existing SIMD entry point in the inventory has a committed `*.asm.txt` artefact in the conventional location, with header recording commit SHA, rustc version, host triple.
- [hard] `dev/bench_results/<date>-asm-audit.md` ships with per-fn verdict and an LTO-opacity comparison across the five dispatch tables.
- [hard] Every "suspicious" or "broken" verdict in the report has a corresponding `type:bug` JIT issue created with cite back to the artefact line range.
- [hard] All gates pass (cargo-ci, code-review, doc-review).
- [aspirational] Audit produces at least one finding that's actionable in a Tier-A or Tier-B task (i.e., the audit pays for itself).

## Non-goals

- Fixing any kernel discovered to be suspicious — that's the follow-up bugs' job.
- Extending the gate to cover non-x86 SIMD (ARM NEON kernels). They live elsewhere and are a separate scope.
- Performance tuning. This is purely a measurement/measurement-infrastructure task.

## Notes

This task was created during session 1 of `babcf05e` after the user asked: "Have we already analyzed any asm that we have in production?" The honest answer was "barely — 2 of 26+." The retrospective audit closes that gap and pays forward into the upcoming Tier-A/B/C work, where each new kernel's spiral step will compare against a known-good baseline rather than starting cold.

Spec doc: attached as `dev/plans/gf2_core_ppc_spiral.md`.
